newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY AT LOW, SEEN SHOOTING UP ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY AT LOW, SEEN SHOOTING UP ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were bid as low as 2.00 percent on Thursday, but dealers said the rate would jump to over 3.00 percent on Friday once the new three monthly credit quota starts running.
"Call money will rise to 3.06 or 3.12 percent bid on Friday," said one dealer.
Dealers said the amount of liquidity in the market was overwhelming as most banks had been saving under the current pact, which will end tomorrow before start of business.
The central bank sets a quota on the amount banks can borrow through its credit facilities at the secured loans rate.
Call money can come under upward pressure if some participants have eaten too far into their quota, but this is not the case this time, dealers aid.
Call money is currently trading well under the secured loans rate, which was raised to 2.50 percent on March 11.
Other rates were a touch higher, with one-month deposits bid at 3.08 percent and three-month paper at 3.12 percent.
Dealers expected that the central bank will announce an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent for the special advances when it sets a new pact this afternoon at 1400 GMT.
"The allocation under the special advances pact will probably turn out slightly lower than the 3.47 billion guilders of the current seven-day pact," said one dealer.
The guilder was somewhat stronger compared to the German mark in afternoon trade, after the Dutch currency was virtually unchanged earlier.
The guilder was trading at 112.3650 per 100 marks versus 112.40 on Wednesday.
